symptoms: Muscarinic (DUMBELS): Diaphoresis/Diarrhoea, Urination, Miosis, Bradycardia/Bronchorrhoea/Bronchospasm, Emesis, Lacrimation, Salivation
Nicotinic: Fasciculations, Weakness, Hypertension, Tachycardia, Mydriasis
CNS: Anxiety, Ataxia, Restlessness, Confusion, Convulsions, Coma

management_steps.details: Universal precautions (PPE). Decontamination: remove clothing, wash patient thoroughly with soap and water. Supportive care of ABCs.

STAT DOSE: Atropine 0.02-0.05mg/kg IV (can be given IM if no immediate IV access). Double every 5 minutes until atropinised ('escalating atropinisation'). INFUSION (start once atropinised): 0.02-0.08 mg/kg/hr (20mg Atropine in 200ml 0.9% NaCl [0.1mg/ml]) using Dial-a-flow or infusion pump, OR 10-20% of total dose already given per hour. END POINT = CLEARING OF RESPIRATORY SECRETIONS.
Check blood glucose. Use a benzodiazepine only (Clonazepam, Diazepam, Lorazepam). NO anticonvulsant agents.
Assess nicotinic weakness (head lift for 10 seconds, hand squeeze). Intubation and supportive management is required if weakness causes respiratory failure.

warnings: If intubation is required, avoid succinylcholine if possible as it causes prolonged paralysis.
